newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Thebe leaves JCI buy consortium.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Thebe leaves JCI buy consortium.

text.p: South African black empowerment company Thebe Investment Corp said on Tuesday it had pulled out of a consortium which has agreed to buy Anglo American of South Africa Ltd's stake in mining house JCI Ltd.

Thebe gave no reasons for its withdrawal from the African Mining Group Consortium (AMG) but said its decision had been taken in consulation with and with the full knowledge and support of the consortium's members.
"Despite Thebe's withdrawal, we remain confident that AMG's bid for Anglo's stake in JCI is a solid investment," said Yaseen Bhayat, a director of Thebe.
The AMG, which is led by Capital Alliance Ltd (Captall), last November agreed to buy Anglo's 34.9 percent holding in JCI for 2.88 billion rand or 54.50 rand per share.
Analysts have raised fears that the consortium may have overpaid for the stake and have expressed worries about its ability to raise the necessary funding.

But Captall chairman Mzi Khumalo, speaking on behalf of the consortium, said: "There is no need for concern -- the AMG is stable. We are going ahead with the JCI deal and will close it on February 28."

JCI gold and uranium division chief executive John Brownrigg said earlier on Tuesday at a results presentation that he could not comment on Thebe's decision to pull out of the African Mining Consortium.
Brownrigg did say that AMG and Captall representatives had been visiting JCI operations.
"The AMG people and Capital Alliance seem to be very happy with what they are going to buy".

Thebe, which is active in a number of industries including leisure, financial services, industrial and aviation and has annualised turnover in excess of 450 million rand a year, said it had confidence in the remaining members of the consortium.
"Thebe continues to support and has full confidence in the remaining members of the AMG...and their efforts to effect growth, efficiency and black participation in the South African mining industry.

Other members of the consortium include African Renaissance Holdings, Co-ordinated Network Investments, Corridor Development Corp, Khotso Investments, Northern Corp Investment Holdings and Women's Development Bank Investment Holdings.
The size of Thebe's stake in the consortium is not known.
